I grew up along the lower Susquehanna river and spent a lot of time trout fishing the trout streams that feed it, so I'm very familiar with what's going on. While conditions have improved, there's still too much manure and raw sewage, along with erosion runoff, that makes it into our waterways. The people along the Susquehanna river don't realize how much damage their doing to industries and jobs downstream. This is largely due to them being bombarded with rhetoric about the evils of regulation and taxes, which drown out any information about the affects of pollution. It's realistic to expect the issue to get worse in the future because of these attitudes.
